column2: Evaluating explanations: An explanatory virtues framework for mechanistic interpretability
column6: Conceptual/philosophical framework (explanatory virtues from four philosophical perspectives) for assessing interpretability explanations; no measured results or observed model behaviours

column2: A mathematical philosophy of explanations in mechanistic interpretability
column6: Theoretical paper proposing the Explanatory View Hypothesis and definitional criteria for mechanistic interpretability; conceptual argument only, no evidence-backed findings

column2: RepliBench: measuring autonomous replication capabilities in AI systems
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: 7 frontier models on 20 task families/65 tasks; best model >50% pass@10 on 15/20 families but complete failure on KYC checks; observed task avoidance and eval-awareness refusals - matches UKAISI-2025-04 (RepliBench arXiv 2504.18565)

column2: How to evaluate control measures for AI agents?
column6: Proposes the AI Control Levels (ACL-0 to ACL-5) framework as an early sketch for scaling control evaluations; conceptual roadmap with no measured results or observed behaviours
Announcement of 20 Systemic AI Safety seed grants (up to GBP 200k each); grant-programme process facts and forward-looking plans only, no qualifying evaluation findings

column2: Adversarial machine learning: A taxonomy and terminology of attacks and mitigations
column6: NIST Trustworthy AI reference report (co-authored with AISI staff) defining taxonomy/terminology and glossary for adversarial ML; definitional standard-setting document with no measured results

column2: How we're addressing the gap between AI capabilities and mitigations
column6: Research agenda/recruitment piece laying out AISI's Safeguards/Control/Alignment research directions; plans and intentions only, no evidence-backed findings

column2: Model tampering attacks enable more rigorous evaluations of LLM capabilities
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: benchmark of 11 attacks shows tampering attack success predicts held-out input-space attack success; state-of-the-art unlearning undone within 16 finetuning steps; robustness lies on low-dimensional subspace - matches UKAISI-2025-03-GOV1 (arXiv 2502.05209)

column2: Fundamental limitations in defending LLM finetuning APIs
column6: Qualifying empirical findings: pointwise-undetectable attacks constructed from benign low-perplexity samples succeeded against the OpenAI fine-tuning API in eliciting harmful answers and evaded AISI's enhanced monitoring - URL exactly matches UKAISI-2025-02

column2: How can safety cases be used to help with frontier AI safety?
column6: Explainer blog introducing the safety-case concept and open research problems; companion to the two safety-case papers published same day; no measured results or observed behaviours

column2: Safety Cases: A scalable approach to Frontier AI safety
column6: Position paper proposing safety cases as a governance approach and outlining open methodology questions; conceptual proposal with no evidence-backed findings

column2: Emerging practices in frontier AI safety frameworks
column6: Synthesis/overview of emerging practices in company safety frameworks (risk identification, mitigation, governance) tied to Seoul commitments; consolidated guidance, no discrete evidence-backed findings

Blog announcing and restating the same-day paper 'Principles for evaluating misuse safeguards of frontier AI systems' (primary, INCLUDED as UKAISI-2025-02-GOV1); adds no finding published nowhere else

column2: Why human-AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
column6: Perspective piece (Kirk et al.) introducing the socioaffective alignment concept for human-AI relationships; theoretical argument with no measured results or observed behaviours

column2: Principles for evaluating misuse safeguards of frontier AI systems
column6: Safeguards Team paper releasing five evaluation principles plus a step-by-step assessment template; largely prescriptive but coded in dataset as a qualifying methodology/governance finding - title matches UKAISI-2025-02-GOV1 (PDF primary)

column2: A sketch of an AI control safety case
column6: Conceptual sketch (Korbak et al.) of how a developer could argue an LLM agent won't exfiltrate data, built on a hypothetical case study; no measured results or observed behaviours

column2: Pre-Deployment evaluation of OpenAI's o1 model
column6: Qualifying joint UK AISI/US AISI pre-deployment findings on o1: UK AISI 36% apprentice-level cyber (vs 46% best reference), 50% software engineering (vs 67%); US AISI 45% cyber solve rate; bio performance comparable to reference models - URL exactly matches JOINT-2024-12

column2: Safety case template for frontier AI: A cyber inability argument
column6: Proof-of-concept CAE safety-case template for offensive cyber inability arguments (Goemans et al., arXiv 2411.08088); conceptual but coded in dataset as a qualifying methodology finding - title matches UKAISI-2024-11
